title: Biology — The Design of Life: Unit Quiz

questions.question: What is the fundamental unit of all living organisms?
options: The atom
The cell
The organ
The molecule
questions.explanation: Cell theory establishes that the cell is the basic unit of life. All living organisms are composed of one or more cells.

questions.question: What does 'irreducible complexity' mean in the context of cell biology?
options: A system that is too complex for scientists to understand
A system that requires all its parts to be present simultaneously to function
A system that becomes more complex over time through mutation
A system that can be reduced to simpler components and still work
questions.explanation: Irreducible complexity describes systems where removing any single component causes the entire system to cease functioning — evidence that the system could not have evolved gradually.

questions.question: What is the role of ATP in the cell?
options: It stores genetic information
It serves as the cell's primary energy currency
It forms the structural framework of the cell membrane
It carries oxygen through the bloodstream
questions.explanation: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the primary energy currency of the cell, produced mainly through cellular respiration in the mitochondria.

questions.question: According to Mendel's Law of Segregation, what happens to alleles during gamete formation?
options: Both alleles are passed to every gamete
Alleles blend together to form a new allele
The two alleles for each trait separate so each gamete carries only one
Alleles are randomly mutated before being passed on
questions.explanation: Mendel's Law of Segregation states that the two alleles for each trait separate during gamete formation, so each gamete receives only one allele.

questions.question: What are the four nitrogenous bases found in DNA?
options: Alanine, Thymine, Cysteine, Glycine
Adenine, Thymine, Cytosine, Guanine
Adenine, Uracil, Cytosine, Guanine
Arginine, Tryptophan, Cysteine, Glutamine
questions.explanation: The four bases in DNA are Adenine (A), Thymine (T), Cytosine (C), and Guanine (G). Adenine pairs with Thymine, and Cytosine pairs with Guanine.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of information flow in the Central Dogma of molecular biology?
options: Protein → RNA → DNA
RNA → DNA → Protein
DNA → RNA → Protein
DNA → Protein → RNA
questions.explanation: The Central Dogma states that information flows from DNA to RNA (transcription) to protein (translation).

questions.question: Which body system is responsible for maintaining homeostasis through hormonal regulation?
options: The skeletal system
The integumentary system
The endocrine system
The lymphatic system
questions.explanation: The endocrine system produces hormones that regulate many body functions, playing a central role in maintaining homeostasis.

questions.question: What is the approximately percentage of energy transferred from one trophic level to the next in an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Approximately 10% of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next. The remaining 90% is lost primarily as heat.

questions.question: According to Genesis 1:24, God created living creatures 'according to their kinds.' How does modern genetics support this concept?
options: DNA evidence shows all organisms evolved from a single ancestor
Genetic variation occurs within kinds, but organisms reproduce after their own kind
Mutations regularly produce new kinds of organisms
Genetics has disproven the concept of created kinds
questions.explanation: Genetics shows abundant variation within kinds (such as dog breeds) but organisms consistently reproduce after their own kind, consistent with the Biblical account.

questions.question: What is Biblical stewardship of creation, as described in Genesis 1:28 and 2:15?
options: Humans should avoid using any natural resources
Humans should exploit the earth for maximum profit
Humans should exercise responsible dominion over creation as God's stewards
Humans have no special role in caring for the environment
questions.explanation: Biblical stewardship means exercising responsible authority over creation — using resources wisely while caring for and preserving God's creation.
